name: lw_15096
statement: (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hp1 : Odd p) {a : ℤ} (ha : a ∉ (⊥ : Ideal ℤ)) : (∃ x : ℤ, x^2 ≡ -(a^2) [ZMOD p]) ↔ p ≡ 1 [ZMOD 4]
closed: ∀ (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hp1 : Odd p) {a : ℤ} (ha : a ∉ (⊥ : Ideal ℤ)), (∃ x : ℤ, x^2 ≡ -(a^2) [ZMOD p]) ↔ p ≡ 1 [ZMOD 4]
informal: Let $p$ be an odd prime and $a$ be any integer which is not congruent to 0 modulo p. Prove that the congruence $x^2=-a^2 mod p$ has solutions if and only if $p$ is congruent to $1 mod 4$ .
type: ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → Odd p → ∀ {a : ℤ}, a ∉ ⊥ → ((∃ x, x ^ 2 ≡ -a ^ 2 [ZMOD ↑p]) ↔ ↑p ≡ 1 [ZMOD 4])
